audits.title: SP9.8 An Audit of Intraoperative Hypothermia Rates in Adults Undergoing Emergency Surgery in a Tertiary General Surgical Unit and Evaluation of the Efficacy of Preoperative and Intraoperative Forced-Air Warming on Achieving Intraoperative Normothermia
audits.setting: Emergency theatre list, tertiary general surgical unit (Oxford University Hospitals)

cycle1.result: Over 18% of patients hypothermic at knife-to-skin.

audits.intervention: Forced-air warming gowns for 45 minutes preoperatively, through induction and intraoperatively (prospective trial).

cycle2.result: 100% normothermic at knife-to-skin; mean core temperature significantly higher (p=0.012).

audits.citation: Foran D, Bramer S, Pledge A, Bond-Smith G. SP9.8 An Audit of Intraoperative Hypothermia Rates in Adults Undergoing Emergency Surgery in a Tertiary General Surgical Unit and Evaluation of the Efficacy of Preoperative and Intraoperative Forced-Air Warming on Achieving Intraoperative Normothermia. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad241.105.

audits.title: A quality improvement project to reduce hypothermia in infants undergoing MRI scanning.
audits.setting: MRI scanning under general anaesthesia, Penn State Hershey Children's Hospital

cycle1.result: Post-scan hypothermia associated with younger age (P = 0.002), lower weight (P = 0.005) and lower pre-scan temperature.

audits.intervention: Protocol development, risk factor identification, vigilance and use of a vacuum immobiliser.

cycle2.result: Re-audit of NICU infants; authors report the problem was minimised (figures not given).

audits.citation: Dalal PG, Porath J, Parekh U, Dhar P, Wang M, Hulse M, et al.. A quality improvement project to reduce hypothermia in infants undergoing MRI scanning. Pediatr Radiol. 2016;46(8):1187-1198. doi:10.1007/s00247-016-3592-0. PMID: 27026025.

audits.title: A Quality Improvement Initiative to Improve Perioperative Hypothermia Rates in the NICU Utilizing Checklists.
audits.standard: Target incidence of perioperative hypothermia less than 25%
audits.intervention: Multidisciplinary team, staff education and a 9-task checklist, with quarterly PDSA cycles and monthly audit of checklist compliance.
audits.other_findings: Hypothermia occurred mostly in the operating room and was associated with emergency procedures; higher checklist compliance correlated with less hypothermia.
audits.citation: Hanna M, Htun Z, Islam S, Hanna N, Kothari U, Nayak A. A Quality Improvement Initiative to Improve Perioperative Hypothermia Rates in the NICU Utilizing Checklists. Pediatr Qual Saf. 2020;5(5):e367. doi:10.1097/pq9.0000000000000367. PMID: 33062906.

audits.title: Improving Safe Thermoregulation Practices in an Urban Outpatient Surgery Center Through a Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.standard: Clinical practice recommendations for safe thermoregulation; target 80% over 8 weeks
audits.setting: Urban outpatient surgery centre, Kirkland, Washington
audits.intervention: PreOp and PACU warming bundle introduced through biweekly PDSA tests of change.
audits.other_findings: The warming bundle was the most effective intervention and reduced staff-perceived workload.
audits.citation: Young JM, Couch K. Improving Safe Thermoregulation Practices in an Urban Outpatient Surgery Center Through a Quality Improvement Initiative. J Perianesth Nurs. 2025;40(5):1147-1153. doi:10.1016/j.jopan.2025.01.010. PMID: 40152849.

audits.title: Prevention of inadvertent perioperative hypothermia as a quality indicator in anesthesia: an eight-year experience from 2014 to 2022.
audits.standard: Postoperative temperature 36 °C or above (hypothermia as a quality indicator)
audits.intervention: Education, tympanic thermometers in all operating rooms, standardised forced-air warming protocols and ongoing monitoring (PDCA).

cycle2.result: Hypothermia rate stabilised between 9.7% and 15.1% (15.2% in 2016).

audits.other_findings: 1902 patients overall over May 2014 to September 2022, 348 (18.3%) hypothermic; about 3.2-fold reduction.
audits.citation: Dogan AT, Artukoglu F, Ercelen O. Prevention of inadvertent perioperative hypothermia as a quality indicator in anesthesia: an eight-year experience from 2014 to 2022. BMC Anesthesiol. 2026;26(1):544. doi:10.1186/s12871-026-04022-4. PMID: 42324460.

audits.title: A clinical audit cycle of post-operative hypothermia in dogs.
audits.setting: Western Veterinary Specialist and Emergency Centre, Calgary (client-owned dogs)

cycle1.result: Postoperative hypothermia incidence 88.0%; 7.5 hours to reach normothermia

audits.intervention: Forced air warmer on all dogs and hourly postoperative rectal temperature until ≥ 37.5°C
audits.other_findings: Hypothermia at tracheal extubation remained high in audit 2 (97.3%); earlier intervention suggested.
audits.citation: Rose N, Kwong GP, Pang DS. A clinical audit cycle of post-operative hypothermia in dogs. J Small Anim Pract. 2016;57(9):447-452. doi:10.1111/jsap.12547. PMID: 27593195.
